page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4a server family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs based on the arm64 CPU architecture and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance type does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, making it dependent on network-attached storage options for persistent data. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on an arm64 architecture, the n4a-standard-2 offers a qualitative balance of resource density and cost efficiency for entry-level workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without the virtualization overhead or credit-depletion risks associated with burstable instances. It is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, microservices, web serving, and development environments that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or high local storage throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is an arm64-based general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, offering 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring predictable performance without the resource contention of shared-core environments. It does not include bundled local storage, integrated GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying instead on network-attached storage for persistent data. Given its hardware profile, the n4a-standard-2 is designed for qualitative cost efficiency in entry-level deployments. It is suited for workloads such as lightweight web serving, microservices, development environments, and basic application hosting that benefit from the efficiency of the arm64 architecture without requiring specialized hardware accelerators.
